at begynde.explanation: "At begynde" means "to begin". To say what you begin to do, add "at" (to) and a verb: "Jeg begynder at læse" (I begin to read). To say when something starts, use it alone: "Kurset begynder i januar" (The course begins in January).

at begynde på.explanation: "At begynde på" means "to begin on". When you start a job, say "Han begynder på et nyt arbejde i morgen" (He begins a new job tomorrow). When a verb follows, use "at begynde" without "på": "Jeg begynder at læse" (I begin to read).

at begå.explanation: "At begå" means "to commit (a crime)". It also goes with mistakes. To say someone made a mistake, say "Han begik en fejl" (He made a mistake). With "sig" (yourself) it has a different meaning, "to get by": "Hun kan begå sig på fransk" (She can get by in French).

at behandle.explanation: "At behandle" means "to treat". When you talk about how someone acts toward a person, say "Han behandler mig godt" (He treats me well). When an office deals with a case, it means "to handle": "Kommunen behandler sagen" (The city is handling the case).

at beherske.explanation: "At beherske" means "to master / control". It is built from "at herske" (to rule). When you keep your feelings under control, add "sig" (oneself): "Han kunne ikke beherske sig" (He could not control himself).

at beholde.explanation: "At beholde" means "to keep". It is built from "at holde" (to hold). When you keep a promise, use "at holde" and not "at beholde": "Jeg holder mit løfte" (I keep my promise).

at behøve.explanation: "At behøve" means "to need". To ask whether something has to be done, say "Behøver jeg at skrive under?" (Do I need to sign?) A very common phrase for needing a thing is "at have brug for" (to need): "Jeg har brug for hjælp" (I need help).

at bekende.explanation: "At bekende" means "to confess". When you openly stand by a belief, add "sig til" (yourself to): "Hun bekender sig til sine værdier" (She stands by her values).

at bekræfte.explanation: "At bekræfte" means "to confirm". When a result shows that a guess was right, say "Testen bekræfter vores mistanke" (The test confirms our suspicion).

at bekymre sig.explanation: "At bekymre sig" means "to worry". To say who you worry about, add "om" (about): "Jeg bekymrer mig om dig" (I worry about you). When you say "you", "sig" becomes "dig": "Du bekymrer dig for meget" (You worry too much).

at bekæmpe.explanation: "At bekæmpe" means "to fight / combat". It is built from "at kæmpe" (to struggle). When you work against a harmful thing, say "Vi bekæmper fattigdom" (We fight poverty). Do not mix it up with "at slås" (to brawl): "Drengene slås i skolegården" (The boys are brawling in the schoolyard).

at belaste.explanation: "At belaste" means "to burden / strain". It is built from "en last" (a load). When something harms a thing, say "Kørsel belaster miljøet" (Driving burdens the environment). When you put your problems on a person, say "Jeg vil ikke belaste dig med mine problemer" (I do not want to burden you with my problems).

at belyse.explanation: "At belyse" means "to shed light on". It is built from "lys" (light). Literally, it means "to light up". When a lamp lights a place, say "Projektøren belyser scenen" (The spotlight lights up the stage).

at belære.explanation: "At belære" means "to lecture (someone)". To say what you lecture someone about, add "om" (about): "Han belærer mig om penge" (He lectures me about money). To tell someone to stop, say "Du skal ikke belære mig" (Do not lecture me).

at belønne.explanation: "At belønne" means "to reward". It is built from "en løn" (a wage). To say what the reward is for, add "for" (for): "Hun blev belønnet for sin indsats" (She was rewarded for her effort).

at bemærke.explanation: "At bemærke" means "to notice / remark". When you say something in passing, it means "to remark": "Hun bemærkede, at det var koldt" (She remarked that it was cold). To make people pay attention, say "Bemærk!" (Note!)

at benytte.explanation: "At benytte" means "to use". It is built from "nytte" (use). When you take advantage of something, add "sig af" (yourself of): "Jeg benytter mig af tilbuddet" (I am taking advantage of the offer).

at benægte.explanation: "At benægte" means "to deny". When you reject an accusation, say "Han benægter anklagen" (He denies the accusation). Do not mix it up with "at nægte" (to refuse): "De nægter ham adgang" (They refuse him entry).

at beordre.explanation: "At beordre" means "to order (command)". When someone with authority sends people somewhere, say "Chefen beordrede os hjem" (The boss ordered us home). When you order food, use "at bestille" (to order): "Vi bestiller to pizzaer" (We order two pizzas).

at beregne.explanation: "At beregne" means "to calculate". It is built from "at regne" (to do sums). To say how a price is worked out, say "Prisen beregnes ud fra vægten" (The price is calculated from the weight).

at berette.explanation: "At berette" means "to report / tell". It is the verb for "en beretning" (an account): "Vi læste hans beretning om krigen" (We read his account of the war).

at berige.explanation: "At berige" means "to enrich". It is built from "rig" (rich). When something brings money to a country, say "Olien har beriget landet" (The oil has enriched the country).

at berolige.explanation: "At berolige" means "to calm / reassure". It is built from "rolig" (calm). When news puts your mind at rest, say "Det beroliger mig" (That reassures me). When a doctor gives a drug that calms, the drug is "et beroligende middel" (a sedative).

at berøre.explanation: "At berøre" means "to touch / affect". When a matter involves many people, say "Sagen berører mange" (The matter affects many people). When something moves you emotionally, say "Jeg blev dybt berørt" (I was deeply moved).

at besejre.explanation: "At besejre" means "to defeat". It is built from "en sejr" (a victory). When you overcome a fear, say "Hun besejrede sin angst" (She overcame her fear).
